tagline: Jazz Fest, Mardi Gras, Frenchmen Street — the most distinct music DNA in America.
summary: New Orleans runs on three calendars — Mardi Gras in February, the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival across two weekends in late April / early May, and year-round Frenchmen Street live music. Tipitina's, Preservation Hall, and the Maple Leaf Bar host the city's signature programming through every other month.
whenToBook: Book Mardi Gras (Feb) and Jazz Fest (late April / early May) hotels 4-6 months ahead — French Quarter inventory disappears first.
travelNotes: Stay in the Marigny, Bywater, or French Quarter for venue density. Streetcars connect Uptown clubs (Tipitina's, Maple Leaf) to downtown.
peakHook: Mardi Gras in February and Jazz Fest's two-weekend run in late April / early May concentrate the city's biggest music-travel windows.

blueprints.title: Mardi Gras
blueprints.summary: Mardi Gras stretches from Twelfth Night through Fat Tuesday, with parades by the Krewe of Endymion, Bacchus, and Zulu drawing global crowds; brass-band programming spills into bars across the French Quarter and Marigny.

blueprints.title: New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival
blueprints.summary: Jazz Fest spans two weekends across the Fair Grounds Race Course with twelve stages of jazz, blues, R&B, gospel, and global-touring headliners.

blueprints.title: Tipitina's Year-Round Programming
blueprints.summary: Tipitina's Uptown stage hosts brass-band, funk, jazz, and touring-rock programming through the year; its Sunday Night Funk dances are a New Orleans institution.
